_comment: Template for each host's /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json (agent-fabric ADR-043 rules 1 and 2), rendered by tools/fabric/managed_settings.py, which fills @ENTRY@ with <prefix>/managed/current/runtime/claude-code/managed/hook_entry.py and drops this comment, and installed by the host's operator as root (sudo fabric-managed install --sha <main's sha>). Rule 1: the built-in guard loads managed mods only, and the session refuses --plugin-dir, --plugin-url and --agents (disableSideloadFlags; rule 7's read-back is docs/live-checks/2026-10-31-managed-settings-2-1-316.md). Rule 2: the fleet's guards are managed hooks, which run before every mod and whose deny is final, each in exec form (no shell: the hook inherits the session's PATH and environment, so a shell or a program found by name would be the login's choice): the pinned interpreter by its absolute path, isolated (-I -S), running hook_entry.py, which runs the root-owned snapshot's guard module in a cleared environment. Matchers, events and timeouts are the workspace settings' as they were. review-fence is new: the review class's tool fence (ADR-065 rule 1), keyed on the payload's agent_type, so it holds whatever the login's agent file says. The transition: the workspace settings keep each guard, made a no-op only while /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json exists and /usr/local/bin/fabric-python is executable, so a host without either keeps its guards as before (a managed hook whose interpreter is missing fails to spawn, and 2.1.316 lets the call through: docs/live-checks/2026-10-31-managed-settings-2-1-316.md), and a host with it runs them only from here. Rule 2 is in force once the file is installed, and nothing is lost before that. Conveniences (the status line, SessionStart, tab-title, model-fallback-note) stay in the workspace settings.
